record.paper_title: Open Questions about Ramsey-Type Statements in Reverse Mathematics
record.original_question: Over ω-models, does the stable Ramsey theorem for pairs with two colors imply the sequential finite-change thin-set principle Seq*(TS^1), namely: for every uniform sequence of thin-set instances X0, X1, ..., is there a single set Y that is, up to finite changes, a solution to each instance?

evidence.quote: More formally, given some theorem P, Seq∗ (P) is the statement “For every uniform sequence of P-instances X0, X1, . . . , there is a set Y which is, up to finite changes, a solution to each of the X’s.”
Question 2.11 Does SRT2 2 imply Seq∗ (TS1 ) over ω-models?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in second-order arithmetic. Recall the following definitions.

- The thin set theorem for singletons, TS^1: for every coloring f: ω → ω, there exists an infinite set H ⊆ ω such that f(H) ≠ ω, i.e., H avoids at least one color. An instance of TS^1 is such a coloring f, and a solution is such an infinite set H.

- The stable Ramsey theorem for pairs with two colors, SRT^2_2: for every coloring c: [ω]^2 → 2 such that for every x the limit lim_{y→∞} c(x,y) exists, there is an infinite set H ⊆ ω that is monochromatic for c.

- For a Π^1_2 principle P of the form "for every instance X there exists a solution Y", define Seq*(P) as the following statement: for every uniformly computable (in the parameters) sequence ⟨X_0, X_1, X_2, …⟩ of P-instances, there exists a single set Y such that for every i, Y is, up to finite changes, a solution to X_i (that is, there exists a finite modification of Y that is a P-solution to X_i, where the finite modification may depend on i).

- An ω-model of RCA_0 is a Turing-ideal: a nonempty collection of subsets of ω closed under Turing reducibility and join.

Question: Does every ω-model of RCA_0 + SRT^2_2 satisfy Seq*(TS^1)? Equivalently, over ω-models, does SRT^2_2 imply Seq*(TS^1)?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not return any source explicitly resolving whether SRT^2_2 implies Seq*(TS^1) over ω-models. Related work in this area (e.g., results on SRT^2_2 vs. RT^2_2 and SRT^2_2 vs. COH by Monin–Patey and others) addresses neighboring problems but does not appear to settle this specific implication. Status could not be verified.

status_evidence.title: SRT22 does not imply RT22 in omega-models
status_evidence.snippet: Monin and Patey establish separations involving SRT^2_2 over ω-models but do not address Seq*(TS^1).
status_evidence.claim: Related separations are known but the specific question about Seq*(TS^1) is not addressed in the located sources.

status_evidence.title: Reverse Mathematics (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
status_evidence.snippet: General survey of reverse mathematics; does not record a resolution of SRT^2_2 → Seq*(TS^1).
status_evidence.claim: No mention of a resolution of this implication in the standard reverse mathematics survey.
